note: Where things stand, separated from what a scenario means. Scenario JSON decides WHICH objects appear and which role they have; this file decides only WHERE the named role is placed, so a new scenario never needs a code change. Candidate positions differ between contexts on purpose: the same prop in 'room' and in 'kitchen' stands somewhere else and the player is put down at a different place, so a day-2 revisit is a changed situation and not a repeated screenshot. Ground level is y = 0 and props are placed so the bottom of their imported bounding box sits on that level. TAV-03 (Issue #10) made this one tavern: the walkable room is 12 x 12 m with 4 m walls, measured on the 4 m grid the KayKit wall models are built on, so no model is scaled or trimmed.

worlds.note: Which content is playable in a run, so the tavern and the older LEX-01 practice room are two authored situations instead of one room that a scenario rearranges. A scenario belongs to a world: the scenario file declares it once and a record may override it. 'default' names the world a normal run plays, and --world <name> on the command line plays another. 'interior' is true for a world built from the interior array below - its furniture stands where it is authored for the whole run and is never rebuilt or moved per scenario - and false for a world with no built furniture. 'staging' decides where a scenario's answers stand: authored_slots puts every answer and every object a situation names at the station the record declares for it (or the world's default station), candidate_slots uses the random pool below. Unknown keys are ignored, as everywhere in this file.

tavern.note: The TAV-01 tavern and the playable content of a normal run. Fixed furniture stands where it is authored; only the small things a scenario asks about appear and disappear, each at a station that means something in the room - the bar counter, the table, the fridge.

legacy.note: The LEX-01 practice room (Issue #2): no built furniture, answers staged on the candidate pool, the guided first example and the beginner briefing included. Kept for regression testing and for practising one action at a time, played with --world legacy.

interior_note: TAV-03's fixed furniture (Issue #10), assembled once per run by scripts/lex01_interior.gd instead of being staged card by card, and only for a world whose interior flag is true. An entry names a model, where it stands, an optional rotation_deg (yaw 0 faces -z, +90 faces -x), an optional 'solid' and an optional 'ground'; unknown keys are ignored, so this section is as open as the rest of the file. 'solid' is set only on the bar counter and the two storage crates, because those are the pieces it should feel like walking into. Everything in the guest area - tables, chairs, stools, lamps, rugs, wall units, dressings, NPCs and every object a scenario can stage as an answer - stays non-solid, which keeps the TAV-02 rule that no task object can block or trap the player. 'ground' defaults to true and stands the model's own bounding-box bottom on the floor; it is turned off for the two wall cabinets, which KayKit models at their hanging height, and for the picture frames, which are modelled around their own centre. Three rules keep a walked-through room free of soft-locks instead of adding a clearance harness: solid footprints sit flush against a wall and in the middle of a wall run, never at an inset room corner; every spawn, candidate slot, anchor and tray point stays at least 1 m clear of a solid footprint; and each spawn keeps several metres of clear straight-ahead walking, since the walking checks the probe already runs walk in straight lines from the spawn and to the inset room corners.

mage.note: TAV-03 role: stands at the storage end beside the crates, between the crates and the tavern table. Same model, label, clips and rotation as the shipped TAV-02 room.

knight.note: TAV-03 role: stands at the west end of the bar counter, so the counter is what makes it read as the person serving. Same model, label, clips and rotation as the shipped TAV-02 room.

gast.note: TAV-03 (Issue #10): the third character, from the same pinned Adventurers commit and the same shared rig, standing at the tavern table. It gives the corpus lemma 'der Gast' a model for the first time. No scenario record calls a character a guest yet, so no existing record's text or delivery_target changes. Its measured model box is not centred on its origin (it reaches 1.09 m east of the node), so at x = 5.6 the model stood 0.74 m inside the east wall; turned to face the table and stepped to x = 4.9 it stands flush on the wall (measured box x 4.33..5.99) at the table's east rim (x = 4.60), which reads as a person at a table rather than furniture inside furniture.

cameras.note: TAV-02 (Issue #9) reads this section as where the PLAYER is put down per context, not as a fixed camera framing: 'position' is the feet position on the floor, 'rotation_deg' is the initial [pitch, yaw, roll] of the eye and yaw 0 looks toward -z. The section keeps its old name because it is the already-shipped per-context framing contract. Every spawn sits inside the room shell, above the floor, and clear of the anchors, the NPCs, the carry tray and the solid furniture. TAV-03 moved them into the tavern: 'room'/'default' stands just inside the entrance at the south door and looks north straight down the room to the bar, and 'kitchen' stands at the near end of the counter run and looks along it toward the stove, so the two framings of a day-2 revisit are two ends of the same room with several clear metres of walking ahead of each.

player.note: The first-person body and its reach (TAV-02). The player is a capsule on collision layer 1 and the room shell plus the interior entries marked solid are the only things on that layer, so no guest furniture, prop or NPC can block or trap them. interact_range is the only limit on what the crosshair can act on: aiming further away is allowed and is answered with the too-far cue, never with an answer or an attempt.

default_stations.note: Where an object stands when a record names it in the situation but does not say where it is. Authored staging reads a placement slot, never a random position, so an unplaced prop still stands on real furniture: everything the player is offered starts on the bar counter, which is where a tavern keeps what it serves, and a bring task then carries it away from there to the table or to a person.

candidate_slots.note: The staging pool of the legacy practice world, i.e. of a world whose staging is candidate_slots, and so of the older LEX-01 records: where a scenario's answers may stand, in the open floor the player walks through, chosen in random order per card so answer position cannot be guessed. The tavern world does not use them; they stay checked against the solid furniture here anyway, because the same room shell and the same bar and crates stand in both. TAV-03 moved them into the tavern: every one of them sits at least 1 m clear of the solid bar counter and crates and clear of the anchors and the NPCs, and each is reachable by a straight walk from the spawn and from the inset room corners the input probe walks to. The review round kept these positions: nudging them apart tightened the biggest answer props against each other (a 3.0 m couch stage and a 2.0 m table stage 2.7 m apart intersect, and the crosshair then lands on the wrong object). The only change measured in was the south-west slot moving 0.15 m off the west wall, because the 3.0 m couch staged there poked 0.1 m into that wall.

anchors.note: Where the surfaces the scenarios place things on stand, and they stand in ONE place in every context: each of these positions is the authored interior entry of the same model, so staging a card puts its things ON the furniture that is already standing there instead of spawning another table or another fridge somewhere else. The two contexts of a day-2 revisit are then two ends of the same room - the spawn moves, the furniture does not - and a context still reads as a different situation because the record puts its objects on a different station. Measured boxes: table_medium 2.00 x 1.00 x 2.00 m centred on its node with the top surface at y = 1.00; fridge_A x -1.85..+1.00 and z -1.00..+0.74 relative to its node, top at y = 2.50; the counter 2.00 x 1.00 x 2.04 with its top at y = 1.00. The fridge keeps its unrotated facing because the placement mode at_front puts an item at the fridge's +z side, which is what 'in dem Kuhlschrank' is shown as, and it stands against the west wall with that side facing into the open room.

on_table.note: Item sits on the top surface of the tavern table, which is authored furniture standing there all run; several items are spread along the surface so nothing is hidden.

on_counter.note: Item stands on the bar counter - the tavern's keeping place and the station every answer starts at unless the record says otherwise. The anchor is the west half of the authored bar run, its top surface measured at y = 1.00, and it is one of the four pieces the player walks into, so an item on it always sits on the far side of a solid piece the player stands in front of.

in_fridge.note: Item stands directly in front of the authored fridge and is highlighted. The committed fridge prop has no door, so 'in dem Kuhlschrank' is shown as 'at the fridge' and is stated as a limitation.

hold.note: bring_deliver keeps the picked object on this tray. It is an abstract carrying state, not a hand attachment, physics or IK: the object simply moves to the tray and the HUD names it. In first person the tray sits between the two spawns and the candidate slots, at waist height, within reach from either spawn, so what you are carrying stays in view.

delivery.note: Offset from an NPC origin where a delivered object is placed.
